title: Compatible derived morphisms lift on varying quotient coefficient sequences
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of the l-adic field, and a scheme W. Let M,N belong to the derived category of modules on the quotient coefficient sequence site [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]. A family f_n: ev_n M -> ev_n N which commutes with every adjacent transition (using normalizedDVRRes on the lower finite map) is the evaluation family of some morphism g:M -> N. No uniqueness is asserted. This includes arbitrary unbounded complexes.

source.place: Tags 0941 and 07A6, with Injectives Tag 079P; the locally finite coinduced two-term argument in this node expands paragraph 2 of prop-coef-integral-dualizing.

proof.text: Identify sequence-site module sheaves with inverse systems M_n whose transitions are R_(n+1)-linear maps M_(n+1) to restriction of M_n. Evaluation is exact. Its right adjoint r_n has zero levels m<n and scalar restriction of M_n at levels m>=n. Scalar restriction is exact, so r_n is exact as well.

For a representative complex N construct 0 -> N -> product_n r_n(N_n) -> product_n r_(n+1)(Res N_n) -> 0. The first map records all transitions; the difference map subtracts consecutive transitions. At level m these are finite products of m+1 and m terms. The kernel is N_m and recursive solution of the m triangular equations proves surjectivity. This proves a short exact sequence of complexes without any exactness assumption on infinite products of sheaves.

Resolve each N_n and, independently, each restricted N_n by K-injectives. Since r_n is right adjoint to exact evaluation, it preserves K-injectives. Products of K-injectives are K-injective. At each level these replacement products have finitely many nonzero terms, so the replacements are quasi-isomorphisms. The short exact sequence therefore gives a distinguished triangle N -> A -> B -> N[1], with A and B the indicated derived coinduced products. Restriction of scalars need not preserve K-injectives and is never claimed to do so.

Derived adjunction identifies Hom(M,A) with families of maps M_n -> N_n and Hom(M,B) with families of maps M_(n+1) -> Res N_n. The induced Hom(M,A) -> Hom(M,B) is the difference of the two adjacent compatibility words. The assumed equations say that the prescribed family belongs to its kernel. Exactness of Hom(M,-) on the triangle supplies a lift M -> N. Composing with N -> A identifies its evaluation with the prescribed maps. No uniqueness or faithfulness assertion is used.

theorem coefficientSequenceDerivedEvaluation_full
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] (W : Scheme.{u})
    (M N : coefficientSequenceDerived l E W)
    (f : ∀ n : ℕ, (coefficientSequenceDerivedEvaluation l E W n).obj M ⟶
      (coefficientSequenceDerivedEvaluation l E W n).obj N)
    (hf : ∀ n : ℕ,
      f (n + 1) ≫ (coefficientSequenceDerivedTransition l E W (Nat.le_succ n)).app N =
        (coefficientSequenceDerivedTransition l E W (Nat.le_succ n)).app M ≫
          (normalizedDVRRes l E W (Nat.le_succ n)).map (f n)) :
    ∃ g : M ⟶ N, ∀ n : ℕ,
      (coefficientSequenceDerivedEvaluation l E W n).map g = f n
